summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, with hands-on robotics hardware experience across Arduino, STM32, Raspberry Pi and NVIDIA Jetson platforms. Built sensor-integrated robot arms and motor-driven competition robots, designed custom PCBs in EAGLE, and resolved 11 hardware integration failures.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.

Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) via a TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping, with TensorRT-optimized YOLO visual servoing (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms).
Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Led the coding team to Stage 3 of DD Robocon 2023 (99/100 in Stage 1); owned wiring, interfacing, and integration across mechanical and design teams.
Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding (2400 CPR encoders) and drove four Cytron motor drivers at 15 kHz PWM with closed-loop heading correction on Arduino Due.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on physical UR5e via UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability measured at <2mm over 10 trials.
Derived DH tables and forward kinematic chains for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
